sentences.en: From NPR, this is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是NPR（美国国家公共电台）的《隐藏的大脑》栏目。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantan.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: If you're living in a city, you may have noticed new buildings popping up.
sentences.zh: 如果你住在城市里，你可能已经注意到新建筑如雨后春笋般涌现。

sentences.en: A high-rise here, a skyscraper there.
sentences.zh: 这里有一栋高层，那里有一座摩天大楼。

sentences.en: These concrete jungles make urban living possible.
sentences.zh: 这些混凝土森林让城市生活成为可能。

sentences.en: They allow millions to live together in close proximity and allow modern economies to flourish.
sentences.zh: 它们让数百万人紧密地生活在一起，并促使现代经济蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: But is there something important missing in this picture?
sentences.zh: 但在这幅画面中，是不是缺少了什么重要的东西？

sentences.en: For most of the last two million years, humans lived in a natural world,
sentences.zh: 在过去两百万年的大部分时间里，人类都生活在自然世界中，

sentences.en: relying on nature for food and shelter.
sentences.zh: 依靠大自然来获取食物和庇护。

sentences.en: The amount of time we've spent in urban dwellings
sentences.zh: 我们花在城市住宅里的时间，

sentences.en: is a small sliver of the total time humans have spent on Earth.
sentences.zh: 只是人类在地球上度过的时间中的一小部分。

sentences.en: When you look at it this way, our shift from forest life to freeways and overflowing cities
sentences.zh: 如果你这样来看，我们从森林生活向高速公路和拥挤城市的转变，

sentences.en: has been very recent and very dramatic.
sentences.zh: 是非常近期且非常戏剧化的。

sentences.en: So how is this shift affecting our health, our mood, and our sense of calm?
sentences.zh: 那么，这种转变如何影响我们的健康、情绪和平静感呢？

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, think deeply.
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》带你深入思考。

sentences.en: We continue our annual summer series, U2.0.
sentences.zh: 我们继续推出年度夏季系列节目“U2.0”。

sentences.en: Authenticity is contagious.
sentences.zh: 真实感是会传染的。

sentences.en: I have been dragged into this all the way, kicking and screaming.
sentences.zh: 我是一路被连拉带拽、极不情愿地被卷进这事儿里的。

sentences.en: Ideas and advice about how you can respond to life's chaos.
sentences.zh: 关于如何应对生活混乱的理念和建议。

sentences.en: Let's do a just check to my inbox.
sentences.zh: 我们这就查看一下我的收件箱。

sentences.en: Just check.
sentences.zh: 就查一下。

sentences.en: Just check.
sentences.zh: 就查一下。

sentences.en: Just check to my phone real quick.
sentences.zh: 马上用手机查一下。

sentences.en: With wisdom.
sentences.zh: 带着智慧。

sentences.en: Ming Kuo has been studying the effects of nature on humans for more than 30 years.
sentences.zh: 明·郭研究大自然对人类的影响已经超过30年了。

sentences.en: She works at the University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign.
sentences.zh: 她供职于伊利诺伊大学厄巴纳-尚佩恩分校。

sentences.en: Early in her career, Ming studied research looking at the well-being of animals in zoos.
sentences.zh: 在她职业生涯的早期，明研究了一些关于动物园动物福祉的研究。

sentences.en: Researchers found that even when animals were provided all the basics of food, safety, and shelter,
sentences.zh: 研究人员发现，即使为动物提供了食物、安全和庇护所等所有基本条件，

sentences.en: they often failed to thrive.
sentences.zh: 它们往往也无法健康生长。

sentences.en: It turns out that zoo animals, first of all, are extremely expensive.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，首先，动物园里的动物极其昂贵。

sentences.en: They die at fairly alarming clips.
sentences.zh: 它们以相当惊人的速度死亡。

sentences.en: And so biologists have studied animals in the wild,
sentences.zh: 因此生物学家研究了野生动物，

sentences.en: and one of the ideas that they have is that there's this thing called habitat selection theory,
sentences.zh: 他们的想法之一是，存在一个所谓的“栖息地选择理论”，

sentences.en: which is that we are wired for whatever habitat we evolved in.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们天生适应我们进化时所处的栖息地。

sentences.en: And so there seems to be this general kind of rule that animals who are in their quote-unquote natural habitats
sentences.zh: 因此似乎存在这样一个普遍规律：处于所谓的“自然栖息地”中的动物，

sentences.en: will do much better.
sentences.zh: 情况会好得多。

sentences.en: They thrive both in terms of physically and psychologically and in terms of their social behaviors.
sentences.zh: 无论是在生理、心理还是社会行为方面，它们都生长得很好。

sentences.en: So if zoo animals thrive in their natural habitat, some researchers have asked,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果动物园的动物在其自然栖息地能茁壮成长，一些研究人员就会问：

sentences.en: could this also be true for humans?
sentences.zh: 这是否也适用于人类？

sentences.en: Given that humans first evolved in the forests of Africa,
sentences.zh: 鉴于人类最早是在非洲的森林中进化的，

sentences.en: could it be that depriving humans of this natural environment
sentences.zh: 会不会剥夺人类的这种自然环境，

sentences.en: has effects similar to housing a zebra in a cage?
sentences.zh: 会产生类似于把斑马关在笼子里的效果？

sentences.en: We'll get to Ming's answer to that question in a moment.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后就会探讨明对这个问题的回答。

sentences.en: But first, it's important to understand how she came to be studying this in the first place.
sentences.zh: 但首先，了解她最初是如何开始这项研究的是很重要的。

sentences.en: She wasn't particularly interested in the benefits of greenery and nature.
sentences.zh: 她并不是特别对绿地和自然的好处感兴趣。

sentences.en: She was interested in the negative effects of noise and crowding.
sentences.zh: 她感兴趣的是噪音和拥挤的负面影响。

sentences.en: The way I got into the research on the effects of the natural environments on people
sentences.zh: 我之所以开始研究自然环境对人的影响，

sentences.en: was I was interested in the dark side of the environment.
sentences.zh: 是因为我对环境黑暗的一面感兴趣。

sentences.en: I was interested in how violent or dangerous or, you know,
sentences.zh: 我感兴趣的是暴力、危险或者说，你知道的，

sentences.en: bad urban environments had detrimental effects on people.
sentences.zh: 糟糕的城市环境如何对人产生有害影响。

sentences.en: And I only got into this by accident,
sentences.zh: 我涉足这个领域纯属偶然，

sentences.en: and then I only came up with this view of the effects of nature through the data.
sentences.zh: 然后我只是通过数据才得出了关于自然影响的这种看法。

sentences.en: So I have been kind of dragged.
sentences.zh: 所以我算是被拉进来的。

sentences.en: I have been dragged into this all the way, kicking and screaming.
sentences.zh: 我是一路被连拉带拽、极不情愿地被拖进这个领域的。

sentences.en: I did not have that view of people that I set out to teSt.
sentences.zh: 我一开始要检验的并不是那种对人的看法。

sentences.en: I came upon that view because I was trying to make sense of what the findings have been.
sentences.zh: 我得出那种看法是因为我试图弄清楚研究结果究竟意味着什么。

sentences.en: I'm glad you said that because, you know, this idea that people need greenery
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你这么说，因为你知道的，这种“人需要绿地”的观点，

sentences.en: or that greenery is essential to, you know, human satisfaction, well-being, thriving.
sentences.zh: 或者说绿地对人类的满足感、福祉和繁荣至关重要这一观点，

sentences.en: You know, when I first heard that, I sort of said, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当我第一次听到时，我有点说，你知道的，

sentences.en: that sounds like a really feel-good idea that I could, you know, hear in a New Age magazine.
sentences.zh: 这听起来就像是一个我在新纪元杂志上能听到的那种让人感觉良好的想法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I find it appealing that in some ways you were a skeptic yourself,
sentences.zh: 我觉得有意思的是，从某种程度上说，你自己曾经也是个怀疑论者，

sentences.en: that for a long time you found this idea to be sort of squishy.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间里，你都觉得这个想法有点不太靠谱。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think like a lot of people, I thought of the environment as, you know, trees, grass, gardens, flowers.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想和很多人一样，我把环境看作是，你知道的，树木、草地、花园、花朵。

sentences.en: I thought of that as kind of a nice amenity, you know.
sentences.zh: 我认为那只是一种不错的便利设施，你知道的。

sentences.en: They're not functional, right?
sentences.zh: 它们不是功能性的，对吧？

sentences.en: They're not what we need.
sentences.zh: 它们不是我们所必需的。

sentences.en: And so it's only when you look at the patterns of what people are like with more and less access to nature
sentences.zh: 所以，只有当你观察人们在获得更多或更少自然接触时的行为模式时，

sentences.en: that you start to see this pattern where, gosh, you know, we see the same thing in humans
sentences.zh: 你才会开始看到这样一种规律：天哪，你知道的，我们在人类身上看到了同样的东西，

sentences.en: that we see in zoo and lab animals, which is the wonderful quote from E.O.
sentences.zh: 我们在动物园和实验室动物身上也看到了这一点，引用爱德华·威尔逊的话说，

sentences.en: Wilson,
sentences.zh: 那就是，

sentences.en: is that organisms, when housed in unfit habitats, undergo social, psychological, and physical breakdown.
sentences.zh: 有机体如果被安置在不适合的栖息地中，就会经历社会、心理和生理上的崩溃。

sentences.en: And we are seeing precisely that in people.
sentences.zh: 而我们在人类身上恰恰看到了这一点。

sentences.en: So when you have people who are, who have a certain amount of access to nature
sentences.zh: 所以，当人们拥有一定程度的自然接触，

sentences.en: and then you give them a bit more, you see better social functioning,
sentences.zh: 然后你给他们多一点自然时，你会看到更好的社会功能，

sentences.en: you see better psychological functioning, and better physical health.
sentences.zh: 你会看到更好的心理功能和更好的身体健康。

sentences.en: In some ways, this argument is saying that humans today, or many humans today,
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这个论点是说今天的人类，或者说今天的好多人类，

sentences.en: are living in the kind of conditions that we used to keep zoo animals in 50 years ago.
sentences.zh: 正生活在我们50年前用来饲养动物园动物的那种条件中。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously, we are doing better by a lot of humans than most zoo animals did in the old days.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很明显，与过去大多数动物园动物的待遇相比，我们对许多人类要好得多。

sentences.en: But I think we are, to some extent, housing Homo sapiens with that same functional view,
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们在某种程度上，是以那种相同的功能主义视角在安置智人，

sentences.en: that, okay, well, as long as they have shelter, water, food, safety, you know, that's pretty good.
sentences.zh: 即，好吧，只要他们有住所、水、食物、安全，你知道的，这就相当不错了。

sentences.en: That should do it, right?
sentences.zh: 这就够了，对吧？

sentences.en: And then anything else beyond that is sort of a plus, and it's nice, it's yummy.
sentences.zh: 然后除此之外的任何东西都算是一种加分项，很好，很赞。

sentences.en: But it's not important.
sentences.zh: 但那并不重要。

sentences.en: I want to take you methodically through some of the empirical evidence that persuaded you
sentences.zh: 我想带你系统地了解一些实证证据，这些证据说服了你，

sentences.en: that this was more than just a feel-good theory.
sentences.zh: 让你相信这不仅仅是一个自我感觉良好的理论。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering if we could start with the studies that you and others have conducted in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 我想知道我们是否可以从你和其他人在芝加哥进行的研究开始。

sentences.en: Walk me through this research, starting with the study that you conducted at the Robert Taylor Homes.
sentences.zh: 请跟我讲讲这项研究，从你在罗伯特·泰勒住宅区进行的研究开始。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, Robert Taylor Homes is a, or was, a series of 16 10-story buildings,
sentences.zh: 所以，罗伯特·泰勒住宅区是一个，或者说曾经是一个由16栋10层建筑组成的住宅群，

sentences.en: sort of along a particular corridor in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 大致位于芝加哥的一条特定走廊沿线。

sentences.en: And they were originally designed with greenery all around them.
sentences.zh: 它们最初的设计周围都是绿地。

sentences.en: But over time, as you can imagine, if you have a ton of kids running around in a courtyard space,
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，你可以想象，如果有成吨的孩子在庭院里跑来跑去，

sentences.en: you don't have much money for maintenance.
sentences.zh: 而你又没有多少钱用于维护。

sentences.en: If it rains, they get mud everywhere, and the grass gets trampled, and it very quickly just tends to die.
sentences.zh: 如果下雨，到处都是泥泞，草地被踩踏，很快就会枯死。

sentences.en: And so, there are very few cases in which the building managers didn't end up just paving over what used to be grassy areas.
sentences.zh: 因此，很少有物业经理最终没有把曾经的草地铺成硬地 pavement 的情况。

sentences.en: And so, if you pave over those areas, you take the trees out, then you just have asphalt.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你把这些区域铺平，把树木移走，那么你就只剩下沥青了。

sentences.en: So, we had this beautiful kind of experiment where people are randomly assigned to different buildings that are identical.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有这样一个绝佳的实验：人们被随机分配到不同的、完全相同的建筑中。

sentences.en: And some of those buildings have a bit of trees and grass around them, and some of them don't.
sentences.zh: 其中一些建筑周围有一些树木和草地，而另一些则没有。

sentences.en: And we just went about studying what the outcomes were in those different buildings.
sentences.zh: 我们只是去研究这些不同建筑里的结果是什么。

sentences.en: And what did you find?
sentences.zh: 你发现了什么？

sentences.en: Well, we looked at a bunch of things, but I think the sort of short answer is we found social breakdown in buildings without trees and grass around them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们观察了很多事情，但简而言之，我们发现周围没有树木和草地的建筑里出现了社会崩溃。

sentences.en: That is to say, when we asked people, did they know their neighbors, did they speak to their neighbors, do they know them on first-name basis,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，当我们问人们，他们是否认识邻居，是否与邻居说话，是否直呼对方的名字，

sentences.en: could they rely on their neighbors for a favor to take care of their kids if they had an emergency,
sentences.zh: 如果他们遇到紧急情况，是否可以指望邻居帮忙照顾孩子，

sentences.en: then the people in the buildings with a bit of greenery were much more likely to say yes.
sentences.zh: 那么住在有点绿化的建筑里的居民更有可能回答“是”。

sentences.en: We also found that the folks who are in the less green buildings are reporting more aggressive behaviors.
sentences.zh: 我们还发现，住在绿化较少的建筑里的居民报告了更多具有攻击性的行为。

sentences.en: And, of course, we had reasons to think this might be the case according to theory.
sentences.zh: 当然，根据理论，我们有理由认为情况会是这样的。

sentences.en: So, there's this attention restoration theory which says that when people don't have access to nature,
sentences.zh: 因此，有一种“注意恢复理论”，该理论认为，当人们无法接触大自然时，

sentences.en: they're going to be more mentally fatigued.
sentences.zh: 他们的精神会更容易疲劳。

sentences.en: So, when you're mentally fatigued, you're also less good at handling difficult social situations.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你精神疲劳时，你应对困难社会情况的能力也会变差。

sentences.en: And so, we thought, okay, if nature is helpful for rejuvenating people from mental fatigue,
sentences.zh: 因此我们想，好吧，如果大自然有助于让人从精神疲劳中恢复活力，

sentences.en: then folks in buildings who don't have any access to nature are going to be that much more fatigued
sentences.zh: 那么住在没有任何自然接触的建筑里的居民就会更加疲劳，

sentences.en: and that much more irritable and that much more difficulty handling conflict in a productive way.
sentences.zh: 也更加易怒，在以建设性的方式处理冲突时也会遇到更多困难。

sentences.en: And what's, of course, when we got these findings, we're kind of like, whoa, you know?
sentences.zh: 当然，当我们得到这些发现时，我们的反应是，哇，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I know the theory predicts this, but I didn't think we'd actually get it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我知道理论预测了这一点，但我没想到我们真的能得出这个结果。

sentences.en: And so, I did a follow-up involving Chicago Police Department crime statistics.
sentences.zh: 所以我做了一个后续研究，涉及芝加哥警察局的犯罪统计数据。

sentences.en: They were very good about giving us two years' worth of crime statistics from another development.
sentences.zh: 他们非常乐意提供给我们来自另一个开发项目的两年的犯罪统计数据。

sentences.en: We wanted to see if this general effect showed up in other Chicago public housing developments.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看这种普遍效应是否也会出现在芝加哥的其他公共住房开发项目中。

sentences.en: So, we looked at a low-rise one instead of a high-rise, and we see the same pattern in police records of crime.
sentences.zh: 于是我们考察了一个低层住宅区而不是高层住宅区，我们在警察的犯罪记录中看到了同样的规律。

sentences.en: So, it can't just be that people living in closer proximity to trees maybe have rosier memories of their interactions with others.
sentences.zh: 所以，这不可能是因为住在离树木更近的地方的人对与其他人的互动有更美好的回忆。

sentences.en: In fact, you know, hypothetically, you're seeing maybe the same amount of disagreement and conflict,
sentences.zh: 事实上，假设一下，你看到的可能是不变的分歧和冲突数量，

sentences.en: but people are just remembering it differently.
sentences.zh: 但人们只是对它的记忆不同而已。

sentences.en: You're saying the police records in some ways provide an objective measure that there actually is less conflict in these buildings.
sentences.zh: 你是说警察记录在某种程度上提供了一个客观的衡量标准，证明这些建筑中的冲突确实较少。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, I'm wondering about other confounding things in the study.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇研究中其他混杂的因素。

sentences.en: I mean, is it possible that apartment buildings with more green space had different numbers of people living in them?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，拥有更多绿地空间的公寓楼里居住的人数会不会不同？

sentences.en: You know, I know the buildings themselves were identical,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我知道建筑物本身是完全相同的，

sentences.en: but is it possible there were fewer people for some reason living in the greener buildings,
sentences.zh: 但有没有可能出于某种原因，绿化更多的建筑里住的人比较少，

sentences.en: and what you're measuring is really related to crowding and not related to green space?
sentences.zh: 而你所测量的内容实际上与拥挤有关，而与绿地无关？

sentences.en: Good question.
sentences.zh: 好问题。

sentences.en: But as you remember, those were the variables I cared about, right?
sentences.zh: 但正如你所记得的，那些正是我所关心的变量，对吧？

sentences.en: So, I wanted to know about, is there more noise, or is there more crowding, or what else is going on in these buildings?
sentences.zh: 所以我想知道的是，噪音是否更大，拥挤程度是否更高，或者这些建筑里还发生了什么别的？

sentences.en: And so, because I was interested, I made sure to measure all of those things,
sentences.zh: 正因为我感兴趣，所以我确保测量了所有这些事情，

sentences.en: and it turns out that those did not explain their relationship.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这些因素并不能解释它们之间的关系。

sentences.en: So, let's just take crowding as an example.
sentences.zh: 所以我们以拥挤为例。

sentences.en: If there was crowding, then it didn't fit the pattern that the violence fit,
sentences.zh: 如果存在拥挤，那么它就不符合暴力事件所表现出的规律，

sentences.en: or it didn't fit the pattern of the green space, or both.
sentences.zh: 或者它不符合绿地所表现出的规律，或者两者都不符合。

sentences.en: I understand there's been research done out of Columbia University and the University of Pennsylvania
sentences.zh: 据我了解，哥伦比亚大学和宾夕法尼亚大学开展了一项研究，

sentences.en: that has explored what happens when you green parts of a city, add more trees and grass to parts of a city,
sentences.zh: 探讨了当你对城市部分地区进行绿化、在部分城市区域增加更多树木和草地时会发生什么，

sentences.en: that this has measurable effects, not just on the quality of life, but even on the crime rate.
sentences.zh: 这不仅对生活质量产生了可衡量的影响，甚至对犯罪率也有影响。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: And the numbers are really pretty startling.
sentences.zh: 而且这些数字确实相当惊人。

sentences.en: So, these researchers worked with the city to coordinate their vacant lot program.
sentences.zh: 所以这些研究人员与市政府合作，协调他们的空置地块项目。

sentences.en: And basically what they did was they designated a bunch of vacant lots as
sentences.zh: 他们基本上做的是将一堆空置地块指定为

sentences.en: eligible for cleaning and greening, quote-unquote.
sentences.zh: 符合“清理和绿化”条件的地块，所谓的。

sentences.en: So, that involves taking out all the trash, little bits of glass, cigarette butts,
sentences.zh: 这包括清理所有的垃圾、碎玻璃、烟头，

sentences.en: cleaning it up, putting in some turf grass, you know, a nice panel of lawn, and then some trees.
sentences.zh: 将其清理干净，铺上一些草皮，你知道的，一块漂亮的草坪，然后再种上一些树。

sentences.en: So, fairly inexpensive intervention.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一项相当便宜的干预措施。

sentences.en: And they randomly assigned which lots would get this intervention and which ones would not,
sentences.zh: 他们随机分配了哪些地块将接受这种干预，哪些不会，

sentences.en: and then they tracked what happened in those lots afterwards.
sentences.zh: 然后他们追踪了这些地块后来发生的情况。

sentences.en: And it turns out that in the lots that received this intervention,
sentences.zh: 结果发现，在接受了这种干预的地块中，

sentences.en: gun assaults go down, by police records, 9.1%, which is really, you know, like,
sentences.zh: 根据警方记录，枪击案下降了9.1%，这真的，你知道的，就像是，

sentences.en: boy, you know, if we have anything that costs any amount of money that can reduce gun assaults by 9%
sentences.zh: 天哪，你知道，如果我们有任何花一点钱就能减少9%枪击案的项目，

sentences.en: in a city, you know, any mayor in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在一个城市里，你知道，美国任何一位市长

sentences.en: is going to trumpet that.
sentences.zh: 都会对此大肆宣传。

sentences.en: And we see similar patterns for burglaries and other complaints.
sentences.zh: 我们看到入室盗窃和其他投诉也有类似的模式。

sentences.en: So, it's a very exciting finding.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个非常令人兴奋的发现。

sentences.en: If I recall correctly, wasn't there a time, Ming, when actually police had the opposite intuition?
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，明，曾几何时，警察们的直觉其实正好相反，对吗？

sentences.en: They actually thought that having trees and bushes could actually increase crime
sentences.zh: 他们实际上认为，有树木和灌木可能会增加犯罪，

sentences.en: because it gave, you know, bad guys, you know, places to hide.
sentences.zh: 因为这给，你知道的，坏人，你知道的，提供了藏身之处。

sentences.en: And in some ways, it made surveillance easier if you actually eliminated all of that.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，如果你把这些全都清理掉，反而会让监控变得更容易。

sentences.en: And that's just that open, you know, open lots or just, you know, things paved over.
sentences.zh: 这就像那些开阔的，你知道的，空地，或者只是铺了平面的地方。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There was that belief.
sentences.zh: 确实有这种看法。

sentences.en: And in fact, there is something to that intuition, but it's fairly limited.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这种直觉也有一定的道理，但非常有限。

sentences.en: So, if you have a lot of, basically, brush and undercover, that can, in certain circumstances,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你基本上有很多灌木丛和低矮植物，在某些情况下，

sentences.en: particularly in park settings, depending on lines of visibility, then yes,
sentences.zh: 特别是在公园环境中，取决于视线，那么是的，

sentences.en: a large bush can provide a place to hide drugs or a gun or whatever.
sentences.zh: 一大丛灌木确实可以为藏匿毒品、枪支或其他东西提供地方。

sentences.en: And at the same time, what we see is that if you have limbed up trees,
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，我们看到的是，如果你有修剪过枝杈的树木，

sentences.en: trees that do not block visibility at eye level, the consistent finding is more trees, less crime.
sentences.zh: 那些在视线高度不会遮挡视野的树木，一致的发现是：树木越多，犯罪越少。

sentences.en: What was your reaction, Ming, as a researcher in some ways who wasn't necessarily looking for this
sentences.zh: 明，作为一名研究人员，你当时有什么反应？在某种程度上，你并不是非要寻找这个

sentences.en: finding and in some ways, as I'm detecting, was sort of somewhat skeptical about sort of the
sentences.zh: 发现，而且正如我所察觉到的，你对自然与这些积极事物之间的

sentences.en: overall relationship between nature and these positive things?
sentences.zh: 整体关系在某种程度上是有些怀疑的？

sentences.en: What was your reaction when you got these results?
sentences.zh: 当你得到这些结果时，你有什么反应？

sentences.en: I mean, to be a scientist, to be a good scientist is to be a skeptic.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，要成为一名科学家，一名优秀的科学家，就要保持怀疑。

sentences.en: You know, so even when you have a theory that's your pet theory, and this was by no means my pet theory,
sentences.zh: 所以，即使你有一个你钟爱的理论——而这绝不是我钟爱的理论——

sentences.en: your job is to try to figure out, is there some way we could have found this without my pet theory being true?
sentences.zh: 你的工作就是去弄清楚：有没有什么方法，即使我钟爱的理论不成立，我们也能得出这个结果？

sentences.en: And so, I'll tell you a related story.
sentences.zh: 所以，我给你讲一个相关的故事。

sentences.en: My old advisor, Rachel Kaplan, who's one of the giants in this field,
sentences.zh: 我的老导师蕾切尔·卡普兰，她是这个领域的泰斗之一，

sentences.en: she did her work for decades in a building at the University of Michigan that faces onto a brick interior courtyard,
sentences.zh: 几十年来，她一直在密歇根大学的一栋大楼里工作，那栋楼面向一个砖砌的内部庭院，

sentences.en: just bricks and gravel at the bottom.
sentences.zh: 底部只有砖块和砾石。

sentences.en: So she spends her career there, 30, 40 years, I don't know how many years, right?
sentences.zh: 所以她的职业生涯都在那里度过，30年，40年，我不知道具体多少年，对吧？

sentences.en: And then, over time, she does stupendous work, and the university finally decides to give her a named chair,
sentences.zh: 然后，随着时间的推移，她做出了惊人的工作，学校终于决定授予她冠名讲席，

sentences.en: a professorship, sort of a very fancy position.
sentences.zh: 一个教授职位，可以说是非常高端的头衔。

sentences.en: And at the same time, they're renovating the building, and they move Rachel into a third-floor corner office in the trees.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，大楼在翻新，他们把蕾切尔搬到了三楼面向树木的转角办公室。

sentences.en: It's right in the canopy, and her office is all windows.
sentences.zh: 它就在树冠之中，她的办公室全都是窗户。

sentences.en: And she says to me, you know, I have been studying this for how many decades, and now I know it's really true.
sentences.zh: 她对我说，你知道，我研究这个已经几十年了，现在我知道这是真的了。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是“隐藏的大脑”。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantan.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹坦。

sentences.en: For years, Ming Kuo has studied how nature affects us,
sentences.zh: 多年来，明·库伊一直在研究自然如何影响我们，

sentences.en: and how the lack of access to nature can lead to crime and social breakdown.
sentences.zh: 以及无法接触自然如何导致犯罪和社会崩塌。

sentences.en: It turns out, this is only part of the story.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这只是故事的一部分。

sentences.en: There's also a relationship between nature and our physical and mental health.
sentences.zh: 自然与我们的身心健康之间也存在联系。

sentences.en: Ming says there seems to be a connection between greenery
sentences.zh: 明表示，绿化与肥胖、高血压和糖尿病等

sentences.en: and health markers for obesity, hypertension, and diabetes.
sentences.zh: 健康指标之间似乎存在关联。

sentences.en: So I did a review of the scientific literature,
sentences.zh: 所以我查阅了科学文献，

sentences.en: and I found every bit of evidence I could that tied greenery to long-term health outcomes.
sentences.zh: 找到了我能找到的所有将绿化与长期健康结果联系起来的证据。

sentences.en: So, for instance, one of the things we find is that
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，我们发现的一件事是，

sentences.en: when you look out at a green landscape, even from indoors,
sentences.zh: 当你望向绿色的风景时，即使是在室内，

sentences.en: your heart rate will go down,
sentences.zh: 你的心率会下降，

sentences.en: and you'll change from sympathetic nervous activity over to parasympathetic nervous activity,
sentences.zh: 你的神经系统活动会从交感神经活动转变为副交感神经活动，

sentences.en: which is basically going from what we call fight or flight into tend and befriend mode.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是从我们所说的“战斗或逃跑”模式转变为“抚育与结盟”模式。

sentences.en: So it has these very systematic physiological impacts on us,
sentences.zh: 因此，它对我们产生了非常系统的生理影响，

sentences.en: which we also know have long-term health outcomes associated with them.
sentences.zh: 我们也知道这些影响与长期的健康结果息息相关。

sentences.en: And I found, you know, dozens of health outcomes
sentences.zh: 我找到了，你知道，几十种健康结果，

sentences.en: where long-term health outcomes had been tied to contact with nature.
sentences.zh: 这些长期的健康结果都与接触大自然有关。

sentences.en: And all of those studies, I threw out anything
sentences.zh: 在所有这些研究中，我剔除了任何

sentences.en: that didn't take into account socioeconomic status.
sentences.zh: 没有考虑社会经济地位的研究。

sentences.en: It is no surprise that we would find rich people tend to have greener neighborhoods
sentences.zh: 我们发现富人往往拥有更绿色的社区

sentences.en: and better health outcomes.
sentences.zh: 和更好的健康结果，这并不奇怪。

sentences.en: I was interested in, let's take two people, same income, same life circumstances,
sentences.zh: 我感兴趣的是，让我们假设两个人，收入相同，生活环境相同，

sentences.en: except for the greenery.
sentences.zh: 唯一的区别在于绿化程度。

sentences.en: And what do we see in terms of health outcomes there?
sentences.zh: 那么我们在健康结果上会看到什么？

sentences.en: Let's talk a little bit about the socioeconomics of this.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈这背后的社会经济学问题。

sentences.en: As you and others have pointed out,
sentences.zh: 正如你和其他人所指出的，

sentences.en: there is an enormous disparity in many countries,
sentences.zh: 在许多国家，存在着巨大的鸿沟，

sentences.en: not just between the rich and the poor,
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是在富人和穷人之间，

sentences.en: but in neighborhoods that are green and neighborhoods that are not green.
sentences.zh: 而是在有绿化的社区和没有绿化的社区之间。

sentences.en: And in many ways, this lines up with disparities between the rich and the poor.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，这与富人和穷人之间的鸿沟相吻合。

sentences.en: Rich neighborhoods tend to be greener.
sentences.zh: 富裕的社区往往更绿意盎然。

sentences.en: Poor neighborhoods tend to be less green.
sentences.zh: 贫困的社区往往绿化较少。

sentences.en: How much of what you're seeing,
sentences.zh: 在你所看到的现象中，有多少比例，

sentences.en: is it possible that some of this is actually just related to differences in wealth
sentences.zh: 有没有可能其中一部分实际上只是与财富差异有关，

sentences.en: that then produce all kinds of other, you know, health consequences?
sentences.zh: 而财富差异进而产生了各种其他，你知道的，健康后果？

sentences.en: Or do you think this is actually connected just to the greenery itself?
sentences.zh: 还是你认为这实际上与绿化本身有关？

sentences.en: Well, that's exactly the concern, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这正是令人担忧的地方，对吧？

sentences.en: We already knew that wealthier people have better health outcomes and more greenery.
sentences.zh: 我们已经知道，较富裕的人健康状况更好，绿化也更多。

sentences.en: So then how do you compare?
sentences.zh: 那你要如何进行比较呢？

sentences.en: And basically what you do is you look for people who have the exact same person A
sentences.zh: 基本上你的做法是寻找条件完全相同的人：A先生

sentences.en: in this green neighborhood and person B in this not green neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 在这个绿化好的社区，而B先生在那个绿化不好的社区。

sentences.en: You want to make sure persons A and B have the same income.
sentences.zh: 你要确保A先生和B先生有相同的收入。

sentences.en: So all of these comparisons in this review I did were taking that into account.
sentences.zh: 因此，我做的这项综述中的所有比较都考虑到了这一点。

sentences.en: One of my favorite studies in this area comes from an analysis of pharmacies in London
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的研究之一是对伦敦药店的分析

sentences.en: and the medications they dispense.
sentences.zh: 以及它们配发的药物。

sentences.en: And there's a connection between this and the amount of greenery
sentences.zh: 这与伦敦不同社区的

sentences.en: in different neighborhoods in London.
sentences.zh: 绿化程度之间存在联系。

sentences.en: What did the study find?
sentences.zh: 这项研究发现了什么？

sentences.en: So pharmacies in London are neighborhood-based.
sentences.zh: 伦敦的药店是以社区为基础的。

sentences.en: So pretty much people go to the pharmacy that's in their neighborhood
sentences.zh: 所以基本上人们会去自己社区里的药店，

sentences.en: and they know how green it is around each pharmacy
sentences.zh: 研究人员知道每个药店周围的绿化程度，

sentences.en: and they also know how many people live there, how many people the pharmacy serves
sentences.zh: 也知道那里住着多少人、药店服务多少人，

sentences.en: and they know prescriptions for mood-related, you know,
sentences.zh: 并且他们掌握了与情绪相关的处方药数据，你知道的，

sentences.en: anxiety disorder medications and depression medications.
sentences.zh: 焦虑症药物和抑郁症药物。

sentences.en: And they just compared for pharmacies that compare the same number of people
sentences.zh: 他们只是对服务人数相同、

sentences.en: with the same rough income, how many more mood medications are they prescribing?
sentences.zh: 收入水平大致相当的药店进行了比较：它们开出的情绪药物多出多少？

sentences.en: And it's substantially larger, the less greenery is around the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 社区周围的绿化越少，这个数字就大得多。

sentences.en: There also appears to be a relationship between greenery and the strength of our immune systeMs.
sentences.zh: 绿化与我们免疫系统的强弱之间似乎也存在联系。

sentences.en: After people spend several days in nature, researchers find measurable increases
sentences.zh: 在人们在大自然中度过几天后，研究人员发现，

sentences.en: in what are known as natural killer cells.
sentences.zh: 被称为自然杀伤细胞的数量有可测量的增加。

sentences.en: After a three-day weekend in a forest preserve,
sentences.zh: 在森林保护区度过一个三天的周末后，

sentences.en: that boosts natural killer cells on average by 50%.
sentences.zh: 这会使自然杀伤细胞平均增加50%。

sentences.en: And a three-day weekend in a nice urban area turns out doesn't do anything
sentences.zh: 而在一个不错的城市地区度过一个三天周末，结果对你的

sentences.en: for your natural killer cells.
sentences.zh: 自然杀伤细胞没有任何影响。

sentences.en: And then if I come knock on your door 30 days later after your three-day weekend
sentences.zh: 然后，如果在你三天的周末过去30天后，我去敲你的门，

sentences.en: and I say, can I have another sample of your blood, please?
sentences.zh: 我说，请问我能再取一份你的血样吗？

sentences.en: And you give it to me, it will show that you are still roughly 24% or 25%
sentences.zh: 你把它交给我，结果会显示你的自然杀伤细胞数量

sentences.en: above your baseline number of natural killer cells.
sentences.zh: 仍然比基准水平高出大约24%或25%。

sentences.en: So it's a big effect and it lasts for a really long time.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个巨大的影响，而且持续时间非常长。

sentences.en: What do you think is going on here, Ming?
sentences.zh: 明，你认为这里面发生了什么？

sentences.en: I mean, is it just the things we see when we're out in nature?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这只是我们置身大自然时看到的东西吗？

sentences.en: Is it things we smell?
sentences.zh: 是我们闻到的气味吗？

sentences.en: Is it just the experience of being out in nature?
sentences.zh: 仅仅是在大自然中的体验吗？

sentences.en: Is it the perception?
sentences.zh: 是这种感知吗？

sentences.en: What's driving these effects, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你认为是什么在驱动这些效果？

sentences.en: Well, the answer is yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，答案是：都是。

sentences.en: It turns out that if we take people and put them in a lab
sentences.zh: 事实证明，如果我们把人带进实验室，

sentences.en: and we just show them pictures of nature
sentences.zh: 只给他们看大自然的照片，

sentences.en: and we watch what happens to their blood pressure
sentences.zh: 然后观察他们的血压

sentences.en: and their nervous system activity,
sentences.zh: 和神经系统活动会发生什么变化，

sentences.en: we can see them become more calm.
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到他们变得更加平静。

sentences.en: So just the visual is enough.
sentences.zh: 所以仅仅是视觉效果就足够了。

sentences.en: Similarly, if I take you into a lab
sentences.zh: 同样，如果我把你带进实验室，

sentences.en: and I spritz what we call phytonsides,
sentences.zh: 喷洒我们称之为“植物杀菌素”的东西，

sentences.en: which are these essential aromatic compounds
sentences.zh: 也就是那些你与树林联系在一起的

sentences.en: that you associate with woods.
sentences.zh: 基本芳香化合物。

sentences.en: So if I spritz you with phytonsides,
sentences.zh: 所以如果我向你喷洒植物杀菌素，

sentences.en: you don't have to be in a pine foreSt.
sentences.zh: 你不需要身处松树林中，

sentences.en: I can see changes in your natural killer cells
sentences.zh: 我就能看到你体内的自然杀伤细胞

sentences.en: and in your bloodstream.
sentences.zh: 和血液发生变化。

sentences.en: So of course, if you're a mad scientist,
sentences.zh: 所以当然，如果你是个疯狂的科学家，

sentences.en: you would say, well, really all you have to do
sentences.zh: 你会说，好吧，实际上你所要做的

sentences.en: is make sure that people's screensavers
sentences.zh: 就是确保人们的屏幕保护程序

sentences.en: are set to pictures of forests
sentences.zh: 设置为森林图片，

sentences.en: and you sort of pipe in some sounds of the forest
sentences.zh: 然后通过公共广播系统播放一些森林的声音，

sentences.en: over the public address system
sentences.zh: 再在空气中喷洒一些桉树精油，

sentences.en: and you spritz the air with some eucalyptus
sentences.zh: 就大功告成了。

sentences.en: and you're done.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你确实会产生可测量的积极效果。

sentences.en: Well, you will have a measurable positive effect.
sentences.zh: 如果我给你维生素D和维生素A，

sentences.en: If I give you vitamin D and I give you vitamin A,
sentences.zh: 那么这解决了你对维生素D和A的缺乏，

sentences.en: then that takes care of your D and A deficiency,
sentences.zh: 但它并没有解决你对维生素B和C的缺乏。

sentences.en: but it doesn't take care of your B and C deficiencies.
sentences.zh: 所以大自然似乎就像一种复合维生素。

sentences.en: So nature seems to be like a multivitamin.
sentences.zh: 你可以从不同种类的接触中

sentences.en: You can get different benefits
sentences.zh: 获得不同的益处，

sentences.en: from different kinds of exposure,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如喷洒气味与视觉效果相比，

sentences.en: you know, right, the spritzing versus the visual
sentences.zh: 或者气味等等。

sentences.en: versus the smell or whatever.
sentences.zh: 但要获得所有的益处，

sentences.en: But to get all of them,
sentences.zh: 你必须亲自去那里。

sentences.en: you kind of have to be there.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，

sentences.en: So I'm wondering,
sentences.zh: 我们接下来要谈谈……

sentences.en: how do you take this multivitamin everyday, Ming?
sentences.zh: 小明，你每天是怎么坚持吃这种复合维生素的？

sentences.en: You started out as a skeptic
sentences.zh: 你一开始是个怀疑论者

sentences.en: and you've gradually come to be persuaded by the evidence.
sentences.zh: 而你逐渐被证据说服了。

sentences.en: Have you found ways to actually apply these insights
sentences.zh: 你有没有找到方法，将这些见解真正应用

sentences.en: to your own life?
sentences.zh: 到你自己的生活中？

sentences.en: I live about a 10-minute walk
sentences.zh: 我住的地方距离大学和校园

sentences.en: from the university, from the campus,
sentences.zh: 大约有十分钟的步行路程，

sentences.en: and I do something which probably looks completely ridiculous
sentences.zh: 我做的一件事在开车路过我的普通人看来

sentences.en: to the average person driving by me.
sentences.zh: 可能显得完全荒谬可笑。

sentences.en: I walk to and from school with my eyes in the canopy.
sentences.zh: 我上下学时，目光都在树冠上。

sentences.en: I fly through the trees on the way to school
sentences.zh: 我在上学的路上穿梭于树木之间

sentences.en: and I fly through the trees on the way back from campus.
sentences.zh: 在放学回家的路上也穿梭于树木之间。

sentences.en: And I have, so my head, my head is up.
sentences.zh: 所以我抬头看着，我的头是抬着的。

sentences.en: I'm probably at danger of tripping.
sentences.zh: 我可能随时有被绊倒的危险。

sentences.en: I look ridiculous, but it makes a real difference for me.
sentences.zh: 我看起来很荒谬，但这对我来说确实大有不同。

sentences.en: And once I started adopting that,
sentences.zh: 一旦我开始采用这种方法，

sentences.en: I have become hooked.
sentences.zh: 我就迷上了。

sentences.en: Ming Koh studies the effects that nature has on human beings.
sentences.zh: 明·科（Ming Koh）研究大自然对人类的影响。

sentences.en: She's a researcher at the University of Illinois
sentences.zh: 她是伊利诺伊大学

sentences.en: at Urbana-Champaign.
sentences.zh: 厄巴纳-香槟分校的研究员。

sentences.zh: 明，非常感谢你今天来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.zh: 与大自然及彼此建立联系。
